definition: `Creature x`: x is one of the things ST I q.13 a.5 calls creatures, which are ordered to God as to their principle and cause. In Lean it is an uninterpreted predicate on beings; only the open premise `OthersAreCreaturesReading Creature p` links it to the primary, by saying that everything other than p falls under it.
note: Stipulated so that STMT-CREATURES-ORDERED-TO-PRIMARY-AS-CAUSE states no more than q.13 a.5 co., which speaks of creatures and not of everything other than God. Aquinas' account of creation (ST I q.44-45, e.g. q.45 a.1, creatio as emanatio totius entis) would source a fuller definition; none is needed by the current results. Broad extension used elsewhere: STMT-CAUSED-IN-BEING-BY-ANOTHER-IS-CREATURE applies Creature to whatever has its being caused by something distinct from it, secondary causes included (ordered to SOME cause of its being), which is wider than this q.13 a.5 gloss; that premise carries the widening. The q.7 a.2 support of STMT-CREATURE-ESSE-IS-RECEIVED covers only the narrower sense (things made by God); the chain deriving 'Whatever has its being caused by another is not INFINITE_1' needs the broad extension.
